speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, flank pain, and fever following your recent antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis. Were the flank pains severe enough to make it difficult to move or lie on your side?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: That's concerning. Did you notice any changes in the color, frequency, or clarity of your urine, or have you experienced nausea or vomiting as well?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cephalexin-induced acute interstitial nephritis.

The temporal relationship between starting cephalexin and the onset of fever, fatigue, flank pain, and rash is classic for drug-induced interstitial nephritis. We need to confirm this with urinalysis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy. REQUEST TEST: Serum Creatinine and BUN.
